reason: The hypothesis directly restates the known result from P1 and P3 that thermal exposure of FeCoNiMnCu (a very similar alloy) forms a protective Cr2O3 and spinel oxide layer that enhances wear resistance, and applies it to FeNiCrCoCu thin films. The mechanism of oxide formation, lubrication, and self-healing is taken word-for-word from multiple passages (P1, P3, P11, P12, P17, P23, P32) that already report this behavior for similar alloys. The intervention (oxygen-rich pre-treatment) is a trivial variation of the thermal exposure already studied in P1 and P3. The hypothesis merely restates a reported result as a prediction.
copied_elements: protective oxide layer (Cr2O3, spinel) formation on FeCoNiMnCu coating after thermal exposure (P1, P3)
oxide layer enhances wear resistance (P1, P3, P11, P23, P32)
oxide film provides lubrication and reduces friction at high temperature (P12, P17, P23)
self-healing/continuous reformation of oxide during wear (P12, P23)
